## Observation

Build time and observation time are separate. The engine declares a
canonical snapshot of the corpus. This layer observes the snapshot: for
the task an agent needs to perform, it returns a path of evidenced hops
instead of a list of matches. Each hop is one fact anchored to a cell, and
the terminal hop is the proposed next step.

The response A(q, σ) to a request q over a snapshot σ is a path, and the
oracle contract fixes four properties:

- Determinism: A(q, σ) reproduces identically on every run.
- Provenance: every hop carries (document, section, cell, build).
- Freshness: every hop is bound to the build identity of σ.
- Gap: when evidence(q, σ) is empty, A returns an open intent.

An open intent is a first-class result. The absence of a path is the next
step: the gap marks the observation to perform or the fact to deposit.

## The canonical chain

A corpus of any size serializes into one ordered chain of cells,
L = (c1, ..., cn). Each cell carries a coordinate, a content fingerprint,
and, under a pinned model, a vector. Content is stored once: a document is
a coordinate interval over cells, and shared units are referenced rather
than duplicated. The ordering rule is canonical, so merging corpora is
commutative.

A snapshot is a manifest plus a chain position, σ = (M, k). The manifest M
hashes the ordered fingerprints together with the model and segmentation
pins. Time travel reconstructs the state at position p as the prefix
L[1..p]. Every projection is a deterministic function of (L, σ) and is
idempotent by construction.

```{python}
#| label: fig-chain-design

}
""")
```

## Path dimensions

Six dimensions feed path weaving. Each contributes one kind of hop.

| Dimension | Hop |
|-----------|-----|
| Structure | Document and section coordinates from chain intervals |
| Meaning | Similarity over cell vectors under a pinned model |
| Time | Snapshot positions and change history between builds |
| Provenance | Source file, commit, and build identity per hop |
| Relation | Validated cross-reference edges |
| Status | Validity, supersession, and contradiction candidates |

A path crosses dimensions. A structural hop finds the section that defines
a term, a meaning hop finds the document that develops it, a temporal hop
finds the build that changed it, a relation hop finds the specification
that constrains it, and a status hop marks it superseded when a newer
source exists. Every hop stays traceable to its cells and snapshot, which
makes the response auditable by construction.

```{python}
#| label: fig-insight-path
#| fig-cap: "One observation: the insight path from a task to its next step, with the gap branch"
dot("""
digraph InsightPath {
    rankdir=LR;
    splines=ortho;
    node [shape=box, style=rounded, fontsize=9];
    edge [fontsize=8];

    Task [label="Task at coordinate", fillcolor="#E8F4F8", style=filled];
    H1 [label="Structure hop\ndefines the term", fillcolor="#FFF4E6", style=filled];
    H2 [label="Meaning hop\ndevelops it", fillcolor="#F3E8F4", style=filled];
    H3 [label="Temporal hop\nchanged in a build", fillcolor="#E8F4F8", style=filled];
    H4 [label="Relation hop\nconstraining spec", fillcolor="#FFF4E6", style=filled];
    H5 [label="Status hop\nvalid or superseded", fillcolor="#E6F0E6", style=filled];
    Next [label="Next step\n(directive or fact)", fillcolor="#E6F0E6", style=filled];
    Gap [label="Open intent\nno evidence", fillcolor="#FFE9C9", style=filled];

    Task -> H1 -> H2 -> H3 -> H4 -> H5 -> Next;
    H5 -> Gap [label="empty evidence"];
}
""")
```

A path that ends at a concrete directive or a validated fact proposes it
as the next action. A path with empty evidence returns an open intent, and
the loop continues: agents deposit facts, the structure thickens, and
later observations find richer paths.

## Semantics under the pin

Meaning is the only dimension that depends on an external model today.
The snapshot contract keeps it deterministic: the model version and the
segmentation rule are part of the manifest, and embeddings are accepted
only under that pin. A structural vector space, where the vector itself
lives at a coordinate, is the planned replacement for this dimension.

## Decisions

- The chain is the primitive source; every index is a derived projection.
- Content is stored once; documents are coordinate intervals over cells.
- Determinism is carried by the snapshot contract: manifest, order rule,
  model pin, and segmentation rule.
- The engine and the observation layer stay separate over one record
  model.
- The oracle is defined by the four properties of the contract.

## Open

- Cell granularity: token, sentence, or segment, uniform or adaptive.
- Projection cadence: per snapshot or lazily on request.
- Semantic introduction: when embeddings enter under the pin, and what
  the structural vector space must provide to replace them.
- Status detection: contradiction and supersession beyond count-based gap
  heuristics.
- Path semantics: what makes a hop valid across dimensions and what
  counts as a terminal next step.
- Product surface and distribution.

## Milestones

| Phase | Deliverable | Evidence |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| 1 | Snapshot contract | Manifest reproduced byte for byte by independent rebuilds |
| 2 | Chain and structure, time, provenance, relation projections | Time travel returns the exact state at a past build |
| 3 | Observation surface | A task returns an evidenced path or an open intent under the pin |
| 4 | Scale and governance | A corpus beyond the reference suite with the same guarantees |

Development starts at Phase 1. A specification for the snapshot contract
will follow this document.
